messages:
julio_support: Customer report — some requests from AcmeCorp are routed to us-west even though they set client region to eu-west1. App sees 300-700ms extra latency. Repro steps below, and we can consistently trigger.

julio_support: repro curl:```bash
curl -v 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?region=us-west' \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' \n  -H 'X-Client-Region: eu-west1' \n  -d '{"input":"hello"}'
``` When both present, routing logs show route=us-west. If we omit ?region param and only send header, route becomes eu-west1.

julio_support: sample routing log (sanitized):```
[2026-03-15T14:02:10Z] req_id=rc-9a3f route_resolved=us-west reason=param_present client_region_header=eu-west1
```

anya_eng: thanks — can you paste a full request-id (sanitized) and the matching router log lines? need to see resolver code decision path. also is SDK setting query param anywhere?

julio_support: posted req_id rc-9a3f above, full log chain:```
router: received req rc-9a3f from ip 3.72.x.x
router: parsed query.region=us-west
router: parsed header X-Client-Region=eu-west1
router: selected route us-west (priority: query)
upstream: sent to cluster us-west-pool-2
```

carol_oncall: hmm — historically query param region was introduced as a quick beta toggle for routing, and we documented header as preferred. But maybe priority changed in a recent patch. adding @bob_runtime to confirm.

bob_runtime: I can repro locally — looks like a precedence inversion PR (RD-4127) flipped the comparator so query > header. That PR was intended for admin overrides but the unit test missed duplicate-key case. Bug: when both are present router returns param.

carol_oncall: customer impact? is it causing errors or only higher latency?

julio_support: only latency and incorrect regional compliance for some EU workloads (data locality concerns). Customer is worried about GDPR posture.

anya_eng: ok. short-term mitigation: advise customer to remove the ?region query param or set X-Redwood-Region header (our internal highest-precedence header) until we fix. Also we can add a gateway rule to drop query.region for accounts flagged EU-sensitive. I can push a config change to temporarily block query.region for that org.

bob_runtime: timeline: I can revert the precedence change or adjust resolver to prefer header again. patch ready (small) — adding regression test for duplicate region signals. Will run CI and deploy to canary.

deploy-bot: deploy queued — job 98123 started by bob_runtime.

bob_runtime: canary deployed to eu-west router group — test results: 12/12 routing tests pass, header now wins when both present.

julio_support: I applied the temporary org-level rule to strip query.region for AcmeCorp. Confirming with customer now.

carol_oncall: thanks, please file an internal incident and link RD ticket. We should also update docs and SDK to avoid sending both.

bob_runtime: created RD-5621 "router: prefer X-Client-Region over query param; add duplicate-header parsing tests". PR merged and canary passed. Rolling to prod in ~20m.

anya_eng: suggested customer message (short): "We observed a client-side parameter (?region=...) that overrode your region header, causing requests to route to US. We've disabled query-based routing for your account and deployed a router fix — please remove the query param from SDK calls. Apologies for the latency and compliance risk"

julio_support: customer replied they see immediate improvement and latency back to normal. They accepted the explanation and will audit SDK usage. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: prod rollout completed for router fix — job 98123 (success).

bob_runtime: closing RD-5621 once post-deploy metrics look stable. Will add an alert that detects conflicting region signals with high cross-region latency.

julio_support: marking support case as resolved, will follow up in 24h. Thanks all for quick turn. :rocket:
